# Sales SQL Analysis — Apparel Brand (Sample Data)

SQL analysis of 12 months of orders for a small Indian handcrafted apparel brand, with a one-page dashboard.
**All data is synthetic**, generated by `generate_data.py` for portfolio purposes.

## Questions answered (`queries.sql`)
| # | Question | SQL used |
|---|---|---|
| Q1 | Headline KPIs: orders, net revenue, AOV, return rate | aggregates, CASE |
| Q2 | Monthly revenue trend | GROUP BY date, strftime |
| Q3 | Revenue share by category | window function `SUM() OVER ()` |
| Q4 | Channel performance (Instagram, Website, WhatsApp, Exhibition) | GROUP BY, AVG |
| Q5 | Top 3 products each month | CTE + `RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY)` |
| Q6 | Revenue by city | 3-table JOIN, COUNT DISTINCT |
| Q7 | Repeat vs one-time customers | subquery + CASE buckets |
| Q8 | Return rate by product | conditional aggregation |

## Key findings
- Festive months (Oct–Nov) bring in about 2× the revenue of a normal month, so stock and ad spend should be planned around them.
- Lehengas and sarees make up about 60% of revenue from fewer orders: high-value products matter most.
- Instagram brings in about 46% of revenue, nearly twice the website.
- Block print shirts have the highest return rate, so check their sizing charts.

## Files
- `generate_data.py`: creates `products.csv`, `customers.csv`, `orders.csv`
- `queries.sql`: 8 analysis queries
- `run_analysis.py`: loads the CSVs into SQLite and runs all queries (output in `results.txt`)
- `dashboard.html`: open in any browser

## Run it
```bash
python generate_data.py
python run_analysis.py
```
Tech: SQL (SQLite; portable to PostgreSQL/MySQL), Python, HTML/SVG.
